To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) we propose a novel change detection approach that is based on deep learning, b) we show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, c) the method is able to detect small changes in the tunnel surface and d) the proposed method is able to handle changes in the appearance of the tunnel surface caused by different lighting, different image acquisition settings, etc.
a convolutional neural network can be used for detecting change between images of a tunnel surface and that the network can be trained using synthetic training examples.
We present a novel approach to the detection of changes between images of the same scene captured at different times, and evaluate it on data collected from a live tunnel inspection rig.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of changes between multiple views of the same surface.
the development of an end-to-end system for detecting changes between images of a tunnel surface captured at different time instances.
the detection of changes between multiple images of a tunnel surface, taken over time by a robotic inspection system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is the best change detection method for this application.
the proposed approach outperforms existing change detection methods in a real-world scenario.
our proposed system is able to detect change in the tunnel environment with high accuracy and is able to outperform other approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a new approach to change detection for long-term, multi-view surface inspection, that can be applied to any surface that has been captured with a camera and is amenable to structure-from-motion.
we have developed an end-to-end system that detects anomalies in a long-term, multi-view, surface inspection scenario.
we have built a system that is capable of automatically and robustly detecting surface damage in multiple views of tunnel surfaces over a long time period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning is a viable and promising approach for change detection, even in the challenging domain of multi-view long-term surface inspection.
a well-engineered neural network can be trained to detect changes with sub-pixel accuracy, and that the network can be trained with a combination of synthetic data and minimal manual labelling.
a well-designed neural network architecture can be trained with minimal human supervision to perform change detection in a complex, multi-view, long-term surface inspection setting.
